newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo Lamivudine may be $5 bln drug - Lehman.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo Lamivudine may be $5 bln drug - Lehman.

text.p: Analysts at Lehman Brothers said on Thursday that Glaxo Wellcome Plc's Lamivudine for treatment of Hepatitis B had the potential to be a $5 billion drug.

In a note issued before the company published what it termed "extremely encouraging" Phase III trial data on the product, Lehman analyst Stewart Adkins said "Lamivudine has the greatest commercial potential of any drug in Glaxo's short-term pipeline".
Adkins said current treatment of Hepatitis B, which the World Health Organisation estimates affects 350 million people, was unsatisfactory and inconvenient.

He said that based on the price of Glaxo's Epivir, an AIDS drug which is a higher dose version of Lamivudine, Glaxo Wellcome could sell its once-daily tablet for the disease at an annual cost of $800 per patient.

"In the Chinese and African markets where around half of the chronic carriers reside, the pricing of Lamivudine will have to be adjusted. However accessing seven million patients at $800 million per annum and another seven million at $50 per annum still creates a huge potential of over $5 billion," said Adkins.
He added that Lehman's own "rough estimate" of sales of $1 billion a year for the drug by 2005 "may be a serious underestimate if the Phase III data is good".
